document.title: U.S. Embassy Kabul Cable 3594, "Looking Beyond Counterinsurgency in Afghanistan"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret NODIS ARIES] Follow-up eyes-only cable to Clinton asking for more time and more options than military counterinsurgency. He notes the 2008-09 troop increase was followed by intensified violence and that more troops would dig the U.S. in more deeply.

persons.role: U.S. Ambassador to Afghanistan; author/signatory of the cable

in a PBS interview on November 7, Karzai sounded bizarrely cautionary notes about his willingness to address governance and corruption

events.description: President Obama laid out U.S. strategic purposes for Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Karzai gave a PBS interview with cautionary notes about willingness to address governance and corruption.
Eikenberry sent Cable 3594 to the Secretary of State proposing a deliberate strategic review beyond counterinsurgency and cautioning against deciding on full troop deployment now.
Karzai was briefed in detail on the COMISAF proposal and explicitly rejected its counterinsurgency basis (two months before the cable).
President Obama laid out U.S. strategic purposes/strategy for Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Karzai was first briefed in detail on the COMISAF counterinsurgency proposal and explicitly rejected its basis and purpose.
Karzai in a PBS interview sounded cautionary notes about willingness to address governance and corruption.
Eikenberry sends cable 3594 proposing the White House commission a deliberate strategic review rather than rapidly approving the full troop request.
Previous U.S. troop deployment totaling about 33,000 after which overall violence and instability in Afghanistan intensified.

key_claims: Eikenberry argues the COMISAF counterinsurgency proposal ignores Pakistani sanctuaries, weak Afghan governance, civil-military integration and U.S. national will.
He contends there is time, into early next year, to decide on the full troop increase rather than commit now.
He cites the 2008-2009 deployment of ~33,000 troops as followed by increased violence, suggesting more troops will not permanently advance strategic purposes.
He doubts Karzai and the ANSF will take responsibility for security or governance, noting Karzai rejected the COMISAF proposal and has a record of inaction on corruption.
He recommends a White House panel of civilian and military experts to re-examine options, including reintegration/reconciliation and pressure on Pakistani sanctuaries.
He warns more troops risk deeper entanglement with no exit short of letting Afghanistan descend into chaos.
